stem: The uterine visceral afferent fibres usually follow sympathetic efferents to which of the following spinal cord segments:
fact: Uterine visceral afferents usually follow sympathetic fibres to the T10–L1 spinal segments, with the source explanation specifying T10–T12 and L1 fibres.
finding: The source displays T10 - L1; PMC supports the conventional T10–L1 uterine visceral-afferent distribution, while the source explanation gives T10–T12 and L1 nuance.

stem: Which of the following parts of the pancreas is intraperitoneal:
fact: The pancreas is retroperitoneal except for a small part of its tail, which lies between layers of the splenorenal ligament.
finding: NCBI places the pancreatic tail at the splenic hilum and supports the source's standard intraperitoneal-tail exception.

stem: The abdominal aorta lies posterior to which of the following parts of the duodenum:
fact: The third part of the duodenum crosses the aorta and the fourth part passes upward to its left, supporting the source key of third and fourth parts.
mnemonic: Aorta behind D3, then left of D4.
finding: The source explanation directly states that D3 crosses the aorta and D4 passes upward on or to the left of it.

stem: The ureters enter the bladder and end at the level of which of the following landmarks:
fact: The source-specific landmark for ureteric entry into the bladder base is the pubic tubercle; the ureters enter obliquely.
mnemonic: Ureter enters bladder near the pubic tubercle.
finding: NCBI confirms oblique ureteric entry into the bladder; the displayed source explanation specifies the pubic tubercle landmark.

stem: The rectus sheath is formed by which of the following:
options: the aponeuroses of the external and internal oblique
the aponeuroses of the external oblique, internal oblique and transversus abdominis
the tendinous intersections of the rectus abdominis
fact: The rectus sheath is formed by the aponeuroses of the external oblique, internal oblique, and transversus abdominis.
mnemonic: Three flat muscles form the rectus sheath.
finding: NCBI directly identifies the fascial coverings of those three muscles as the rectus sheath.

stem: The renal arteries arise from the abdominal aorta just posterior to which of the following structures:
fact: The renal arteries arise from the abdominal aorta just inferior to the superior mesenteric artery origin and posterior to the pancreas.
finding: NCBI states that renal arteries arise just inferior to the SMA origin and are posterior to the pancreas.

stem: Which of the following best describes the location of the omental bursa:
options: To the right of the oblique attachment of the mesentery
Posterior to the stomach and liver
Anterior to the stomach and liver
fact: The omental bursa, or lesser sac, lies posterior to the stomach and liver and anterior to the pancreas.
mnemonic: Lesser sac: behind stomach, ahead of pancreas.
finding: The source explanation gives the full relation; NCBI corroborates the peritoneal framework and communication of greater and lesser sacs through the epiploic foramen.

stem: The infraduodenal region of the common bile duct:
options: runs in a groove posterior to the head of the pancreas.
lies posterior to the first part of the duodenum.
lies posterior to the inferior vena cava.
lies anterior to the left renal vein.
empties into the third part of the duodenum.
fact: The infraduodenal common bile duct runs in a groove on the posterior surface of the pancreatic head and is anterior to the inferior vena cava.
mnemonic: Distal bile duct: groove behind pancreatic head.
finding: NCBI supports the distal common bile duct's pancreatic-head relationship; the source explanation specifies the right renal vein and IVC relations.

stem: Which of the following structures is NOT a posterior relation of the transverse colon:
fact: The spleen lies superior to the left colic flexure rather than being a posterior relation of the transverse colon in the source's listed anatomy.
mnemonic: Transverse colon behind: D2, pancreatic head, mesentery, DJ flexure, not spleen.
finding: The source explanation lists the first four structures posteriorly and places the spleen superior to the left colic flexure.

stem: The abdominal aorta terminates as which of the following:
options: Right and left common iliac arteries
fact: The abdominal aorta terminates by bifurcating into the right and left common iliac arteries.
mnemonic: Aorta ends as two common iliacs.
finding: NCBI states that the abdominal aorta bifurcates into the right and left common iliac arteries at L4.
